 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2026-CV-0039
 Zachary Arnold, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Zachary Arnold
Date:
November 9, 2026
Location:
Offices of Gardner & Morris Law Group
Examining attorney:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Sergio Acosta, Gardner & Morris Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's okay. You can use the case caption.
Q: That's fine. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work, heading south on a main road in League City, Texas. Traffic had slowed for a light ahead of
me.
Q: Walk me through what happened right before the impact.
A: I came to a stop behind a sedan at the light. I had my foot on the brake and I was looking at the signal. The next thing I knew, I
felt a hard jolt from behnid and my head snapped forward.
Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you?
A: Only in the mirror, just before. It was a pickup truck, and it looked like it wasn't slowing down.
Q: After the collision, what did you do?
A: I sat there for a moment. My right hand was pressed against the steering wheel and the pain shot up my arm almost
immediately. I got out, checked on the driver ahead of me, and then called the police.
Q: When did you first seek medical care?
A: That evening. My wrist was swelling and I couldn't close my hand. A friend drove me to an urgent care clinic, and they sent
me for X-rays the next day.
Q: What did the imaging show?
A: A fracture in the wrist, on the right side. The doctor explained that it was a break near the end of the radius bone.
Q: What treatment did you receive?
A: They put me in a cast for about six weeks. Then I went to physical therapy twice a week for several months to regain grip
strength and range of motion.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Pretty significantly. I'm right-handed, so simple things like buttoning a shirt, cooking, or typing for long stretches were hard
for a long time. I had to hire someone to help with yard work, and I stopped playing the weekly tennis league I'd been in for
years.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Some. When the weather turns cold, my wrist aches and I lose grip strength by the end of the day. I still do my home exercises
most mornings.
Q: Thank you. Nothing further at this time.
</page>
